main_text.head: VALOR ORACULI PRÆSENTIS, Ut querelæ PROPOSITÆ Solidè respondentis, DEMONSTRATUS.
main_text.p: §. 1.PRout in istâ querelâ continebatur accu-satio quorundam, in populo prævalen-tium: ita accusationi respondet in hoc oraculo sententia Dei, contra accusatos prolata: quam quasi ex cœlo à tribunali Dei secum allatam cum justis in populo Dei communicat atque contra impios & violentos justorum oppressores promulgat propheta, quâ accusatio illa justificatur. Enarraverat Vates, causidicum agens, veluti in libello supplici causam justorum, & quæ pro causâ illâ passi fuerant ab impiis, qui arguebantur vani-tatis & laboris. Judex confirmat illud, & tanquam re-atum condemnat, exponens illud esse vim suam habere pro Deo suo, & gloriam suam alienare à se, atque sacrilegè rapere: dum veram salutem & justitiam ignorantes ex lege & cæremoniis quærunt justificari; atque tyran-

page.notes: The ornamental drop-cap P is partly obscured; the letter after it reads "R" but is not fully clear, so the initial word is given as printed "PRout". A dark blot covers part of "pro" in "promulgat"; the reading "promulgat" is uncertain and should be checked against another copy. Long s is rendered as plain s throughout (e.g. "causidicum", "causam"). Italic words are marked where visible. The word-break "tyran-" at the foot continues on the next page.
